conventions.tracks: Skeleton3D:<bone> position/rotation, 30 fps keys, only the channels the source keys (+ main-hand prop tracks on the guard clips, see added_prop_tracks)

weapon.blade: saber / tomahawk / knife in the machete clips (group machete, machete-draw): the Actor_A machete prop frames are converted to Actor_B's own knife frame (weapon_frames.py `blade`): the blade leaves the fist along the prop bone's +Y, the edge / finger side about -Z, origin at the fist centre. Attach the saber with saber_model.md's SABER_PROP_OFFSET, the same offset as in Actor_B's native knife clips.
weapon.two_hand: spear, club and musket in the guard, haft sweep, club, blocked and butt-stroke clips (groups two-hand-guard, two-hand-club, musket-butt): +Z runs along the weapon from the left (lower) hand through the right hand to the working end (spear point, club head, musket butt); the left palm grips about 0.08 m up +Z from the origin. The roll about +Z is set from the right palm (the canonical right-hand grip swung onto the axis): the haft and club clips (atk-pipe-*, whose source prop is a round pipe with no authored roll) and the guard clips keep one roll in the fist, so a roll-asymmetric weapon (musket lock, club head, bayonet) attaches with one offset; the long-gun clips (atk-lg-*) keep the source rifle's roll. Haft clips hold the weapon in a bat grip (right palm about 0.2 m up); atk-pipe-block and the pipe-block-* clips key no prop in the source and get the weapon where the source's two hands hold it (synthetic_grip: the axis through both hands' grip points, the off hand at the source's placement relative to the right hand, scaled; right palm about 0.45 m up in the guard); in the one-handed recoil of atk-pipe-block it eases to the bat grip.
weapon.other: fist, pistol / bow quick melee and the crawl clips key the prop bones as in the source (world rotation copied); clips listed with prop_far_from_palm_m use the prop bones for something other than a held weapon.

conventions.ground: clip origin = floor point under the character (pelvis and stride scaled by scale_s; legs by leg_ratio from the hip, hands on the floor by arm_ratio from the shoulder)
conventions.horse: clip origin = saddle attach point (horse.md 1.2); rider seat and stirrups calibrated on actor_b-horse-idle (rider clips are saddle-relative: another saddle height needs no change; foot IK to the stirrups)
conventions.mount: Mount clips are baked into the saddle frame (retarget.diag.mount_align): the clip origin is the saddle attach point of the horse for the whole clip, and the root carries the solved ground -> saddle align. During the ground phase the floor lies reference_saddle_height_m below the origin (the fitted source ground scaled by s, raised by the rider's standing offset, standing_offset_m: the source stands about 3 cm above its fitted ground, so the planted push-off ball and the feet of the first frame are at their bind contact height on this floor). Runtime recipe for a horse whose saddle attach point is H above the ground: place the rider's skeleton at the saddle attach point and shift it down (along the saddle's up axis) by (H - reference_saddle_height_m) x (1 - ground_to_saddle[frame]). ground_to_saddle is 0 until the push-off foot leaves the ground (so the planted foot is exact on the real floor), then rises to 1 while that foot is in the air. Foot IK the stirrup foot to the horse's stirrup and the hands to the pommel / reins while the difference is being taken up. start_ground_pose gives where the rider stands (x, z in the saddle frame, floor) and faces (yaw) at the first frame: move the player there before the clip starts.
conventions.loop: loop: true = a real cycle the runtime loops (seam closed by the tool); seamless: the source's first and last poses match (not a loop by itself). loop_mode is copied from the source (0).
